items.s: Double cut file: a file with two sets of crossing teeth that removes metal faster. The other options describe Shear, Reaming, Filing.

Ball pein hammer
Try square
Divider

items.q: In this course, Brazing refers to
o: welding in which a flame from burning fuel gas and oxygen supplies the heat
joining metals with a filler that melts above four hundred and fifty degrees but below the parent metal
the material that cleans the surfaces and helps the filler to flow during soldering or brazing
a headed pin passed through holes and hammered to join two plates
items.s: Brazing: joining metals with a filler that melts above four hundred and fifty degrees but below the parent metal. The other options describe Gas welding, Rivet, Flux.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Single cut file.

the saw used to cut metal bar and section to length
a file with teeth in one direction used for finishing and sharpening
enlarging a drilled hole slightly to make it accurate and smooth

items.q: In this course, Surface plate refers to

laying out the shape and positions of features on a workpiece before cutting
a calliper with one bent leg used to scribe lines parallel to an edge
a flat reference plate on which work is marked out and checked for flatness
items.s: Surface plate: a flat reference plate on which work is marked out and checked for flatness. The other options describe Marking out, Vee block, Odd leg calliper.

the cover fitted over moving parts to prevent contact and injury
the arrangement of machines, benches and stores so that work flows safely and without obstruction
a written rule that governs conduct and safe practice in the workshop

Die
Drilling

a hardened pointed tool used to scribe fine layout lines on metal
a precision instrument that measures small thicknesses and diameters to hundredths of a millimetre

the protective eyewear worn to keep chips and dust out of the eyes

the marked container holding the materials needed to treat minor injuries

the gradual change of diameter along the length of a workpiece
the rate at which the surface of the work passes the cutting tool, in metres per minute
